title: HEO and Quantum Aero to Integrate Non-Earth Imaging into CAIMAN for Space Domain Awareness
summary: HEO and Quantum Aero to Integrate Non-Earth Imaging into CAIMAN for Space Domain Awareness
body_markdown:
SYDNEY, Australia (November 6, 2026) – HEO announced plans to integrate its Non-Earth Imaging (NEI) data and insights into Quantum Aero’s mission-adaptive AI command and control platform, QA-CAIMAN (C2 AI Mission Adaptive Node), to develop a dedicated space domain awareness module. Quantum Aero is a defence AI startup focused on next-generation security innovation.


Under the cooperation, HEO will provide NEI imagery and related data relevant to Korea's space domain awareness requirements. Quantum Aero will integrate these inputs into CAIMAN to help users interpret observations of space objects and incorporate that information into their operational assessment and decision-making workflows.


Non-Earth imaging uses cameras in space to observe other satellites and orbital objects. These observations provide visual evidence of spacecraft identity, configuration, condition, capabilities, and behaviour, adding information that can complement other sources of space-domain data.


Quantum Aero is developing a space module for QA-CAIMAN alongside its other mission modules, including anti-submarine warfare, logistics and counter-terrorism. The space module displays space objects in three dimensions and provides orbital information, event history and attitude information. Combined with HEO's NEI data and insights, it will support satellite identification and characterization, comparison of observations over time, and analyst assessment of visible changes in spacecraft configuration or condition, allowing users to review these space-domain observations alongside other information in their C2 environment.


*QA-CAIMAN space domain awareness module (Image: Quantum Aero)*


‍


"Space domain awareness becomes more useful when it is connected to the systems people use to understand situations and make decisions," said Kim Kang, Director of Business Development at Quantum Aero. "By integrating HEO's data & insights into CAIMAN, we aim to give Korean users a clearer understanding of activity in orbit and make that understanding part of their operational workflow. This cooperation is an important step in extending CAIMAN's capabilities into the space domain."


The collaboration combines HEO's expertise in imaging and interpreting objects in orbit with Quantum Aero's defense AI development and local integration capabilities. For HEO, it will establish an additional application for its space-based intelligence within a Korean C2 product environment.


"Non-Earth imaging helps users understand what is happening to objects in space, providing visual evidence of their identity, configuration and capabilities," said Hiranya Jayakody, CTO & Co-Founder of HEO. "Working with Quantum Aero, HEO will bring those observations into CAIMAN, helping Korean users connect visual information about satellites with their broader space domain awareness needs."


Building on their existing cooperation, the companies aim to make space-based observations more accessible and useful to Korean government, defense and commercial space users.


‍


**About HEO**


HEO is building the intelligence layer for space. We image objects in orbit on demand, turning existing satellites into inspection platforms and building our own sensors where coverage gaps remain. Our software automates tasking, capture and analysis, turning imagery into insight about the condition, configuration and behaviour of objects in orbit. HEO operates internationally, with offices in Australia, France, Japan, the United Kingdom and the United States. Our goal is to make any image in the Solar System available on demand.
